evidence.claim: From the Virgin River floodplain to sagebrush beneath sandstone summits.
evidence.quote: from the Virgin River floodplain, through pinyon-juniper woodlands, to sagebrush desert

evidence.claim: From the Virgin River floodplain to sagebrush beneath sandstone summits.
evidence.quote: views along the route include Smithsonian Butte, Eagle Crags, Vermilion Cliffs within the Canaan Mountain Wilderness, and the prominent sandstone pinnacles of Zion National Park.

evidence.claim: Smithsonian Butte Back Country Byway crosses 9.25 miles between Rockville and Apple Valley, just south of Zion National Park.
evidence.quote: Smithsonian Butte Back Country Byway travels for 9.25 miles between Rockville and Apple Valley, Utah, just south of Zion National Park.

evidence.claim: The landscape changes from the Virgin River floodplain to pinyon-juniper woodland and then sagebrush desert.
evidence.quote: from the Virgin River floodplain, through pinyon-juniper woodlands, to sagebrush desert

evidence.claim: The Bureau of Land Management highlights views of Smithsonian Butte, Eagle Crags, the Vermilion Cliffs and Zion’s sandstone pinnacles along this back country byway.
evidence.quote: Spectacular views along the route include Smithsonian Butte, Eagle Crags, Vermilion Cliffs within the Canaan Mountain Wilderness, and the prominent sandstone pinnacles of Zion National Park.

evidence.claim: Rockville Bridge supplied a connection for an earlier generation of park touring.
evidence.quote: The bridge was built for the National Park Service in 1924 to provide a link between Zion National Park and the North Rim area of Grand Canyon National Park.

evidence.claim: Built for the National Park Service in 1924, it linked Zion with the Grand Canyon’s North Rim, allowing motorists to make a circular tour through southern Utah and northern Arizona.
evidence.quote: The bridge was built for the National Park Service in 1924 to provide a link between Zion National Park and the North Rim area of Grand Canyon National Park. The new bridge allowed motorists to take a circular tour of the national parks in southern Utah and northern Arizona.

evidence.claim: The Bureau of Public Roads designed it, a Minneapolis company fabricated the steel, and Ogden contractor C. F. Dinsmore erected it.
evidence.quote: The bridge was designed by the U.S. Bureau of Public Roads for the Park Service, fabricated by the Minneapolis Steel and Machinery Company, and erected by Ogden contractor C. F. Dinsmore.

evidence.claim: From Rockville, Bridge Road leads south to Grafton Road and the byway.
evidence.quote: From Rockville, UT (north): Turn south on Bridge Road. After 0.3 miles, continue around sharp righthand turn onto 250 South/Grafton Road. In 1.3 miles, turn left onto Smithsonian Butte National Back Country Byway.

evidence.claim: A side trip reaches Grafton’s rehabilitated buildings and interpretive information.
evidence.quote: A short side trip of approximately 1.8 miles (3.6 miles round trip) leads to the historic ghost town of Grafton

evidence.claim: A side trip reaches Grafton’s rehabilitated buildings and interpretive information.
evidence.quote: Several rehabilitated buildings and interpretive information

evidence.claim: The main route continues through woodland to the sagebrush of Big Plain Junction at Highway 59.
evidence.quote: through pinyon-juniper woodlands, to sagebrush desert at the Big Plain Junction of Highway 59.

evidence.claim: The route often becomes impassable during heavy rain and inclement winter weather. No services are available along the byway.
evidence.quote: This route often becomes impassable during heavy rain and periods of inclement winter weather. No services are available along the Byway.

evidence.claim: A single 217-foot steel span crosses the Virgin River at Rockville.
evidence.quote: The Rockville Bridge spans the east fork of the Virgin River in Rockville

evidence.claim: A single 217-foot steel span crosses the Virgin River at Rockville.
evidence.quote: The bridge spans 217 feet (66 m) in a single span, using a steel twelve-panel Parker through-truss.

evidence.claim: Its twelve-panel Parker through-truss belongs to the bridge built for the National Park Service in 1924.
evidence.quote: The bridge was built for the National Park Service in 1924

evidence.claim: Its twelve-panel Parker through-truss belongs to the bridge built for the National Park Service in 1924.
evidence.quote: using a steel twelve-panel Parker through-truss.

evidence.claim: The crossing connected Zion National Park with the Grand Canyon’s North Rim for motorists making a circular tour of the region’s parks.
evidence.quote: to provide a link between Zion National Park and the North Rim area of Grand Canyon National Park. The new bridge allowed motorists to take a circular tour of the national parks in southern Utah and northern Arizona.

evidence.claim: Minneapolis Steel and Machinery Company fabricated it; C. F. Dinsmore, an Ogden contractor, erected it.
evidence.quote: fabricated by the Minneapolis Steel and Machinery Company, and erected by Ogden contractor C. F. Dinsmore.

evidence.claim: The bridge entered the National Register of Historic Places in 1995.
evidence.quote: The Rockville Bridge was placed on the National Register of Historic Places in 1995.

evidence.claim: Grafton’s irrigation ditches demanded attention at least weekly: silt from the Virgin River repeatedly clogged them.
evidence.quote: One particular challenge to farming was the large amounts of silt in Grafton's section of the Virgin River. Residents had to dredge out clogged irrigation ditches at least weekly

evidence.claim: Flooding also discouraged resettlement, and most residents eventually moved to more accessible places across the river.
evidence.quote: Continued severe flooding discouraged resettlement, and most of the population moved permanently to more accessible locations on the other side of the river.

evidence.claim: In 1997, the Grafton Heritage Partnership organized to preserve the historic townsite.
evidence.quote: In June 1997, the Grafton Heritage Partnership was organized to protect, preserve, and restore the Grafton Townsite.

evidence.claim: Restoration included the old church and several homes, with replacement windows, doors and roofing.
evidence.quote: the old church, Russell Home, Louisa Foster Home, the Berry fence in the cemetery, and John Wood home were restored, with new windows, doors, roofing

evidence.claim: The BLM identifies rehabilitated buildings and interpretive information on this side trip from the byway.
evidence.quote: Several rehabilitated buildings and interpretive information provide a glimpse into early pioneer life along the Virgin River.

evidence.claim: Light-colored Navajo Sandstone caps the deep-red Kayenta Formation on Smithsonian Butte.
evidence.quote: The uppermost part of this mountain is composed of light-colored Jurassic Navajo Sandstone which overlays the deep-red sandstone of the Kayenta Formation.

evidence.claim: The 6,780-foot summit lies in the Canaan Mountain Wilderness, four miles southwest of Rockville.
evidence.quote: Smithsonian Butte is a 6,780-foot (2,070 m) elevation summit located in the Canaan Mountain Wilderness

evidence.claim: The 6,780-foot summit lies in the Canaan Mountain Wilderness, four miles southwest of Rockville.
evidence.quote: Smithsonian Butte is situated four miles (6.4 km) southwest of Rockville

evidence.claim: Geologist Clarence Edward Dutton named it for the Smithsonian Institution, which sponsored an exploration of the region.
evidence.quote: This geographical feature was named by geologist Clarence Edward Dutton (1841–1912) for the Smithsonian Institution which had sponsored an exploration of the region

evidence.claim: His field party mapped 12,000 square miles of southern Utah’s high plateaus between 1875 and 1877.
evidence.quote: From 1875 to 1877, Dutton's field party mapped 12,000 square miles (31,000 km2) of the high plateaus of southern Utah.

evidence.claim: The U.S. Board on Geographic Names formally adopted the butte’s name in 1934.
evidence.quote: the toponym was officially adopted in 1934 by the U.S. Board on Geographic Names.

evidence.claim: Pale sandstone above deep-red layers marks the upper part of Smithsonian Butte.
evidence.quote: The uppermost part of this mountain is composed of light-colored Jurassic Navajo Sandstone which overlays the deep-red sandstone of the Kayenta Formation.

evidence.claim: Before the bridge, the butte already carried a name from scientific exploration: geologist Clarence Edward Dutton named it for the Smithsonian Institution, sponsor of an exploration of the region.
evidence.quote: This geographical feature was named by geologist Clarence Edward Dutton (1841–1912) for the Smithsonian Institution which had sponsored an exploration of the region

evidence.claim: Gooseberry, Grafton and Wire Mesas lie east of the byway, with trails for non-motorized recreation.
evidence.quote: East of the Byway, Gooseberry, Grafton, and Wire Mesas provide an extensive network of trails for non-motorized recreation.

evidence.claim: Rockville retains one of Utah’s last surviving examples of this rigid Parker through-truss bridge type.
evidence.quote: one of the last surviving examples of a rigid Parker through truss bridge in the state of Utah.

evidence.claim: The preservation effort also purchased 150 acres of farmland, where agricultural operations maintain the site’s farming appearance.
evidence.quote: 150 acres (61 ha) of farmland were purchased, on which agricultural operations are performed to enhance the farming appearance.

evidence.claim: On its north side, the mountain rises 3,000 feet above the Virgin River in three miles; the saddle to Canaan Mountain bears Dutton’s name.
evidence.quote: 3,000 feet in three miles above the Virgin River on its north aspect

evidence.claim: On its north side, the mountain rises 3,000 feet above the Virgin River in three miles; the saddle to Canaan Mountain bears Dutton’s name.
evidence.quote: The saddle between Smithsonian Butte and its parent Caanan Mountain is named Dutton Pass, after him.
